02. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned Additional Standing Counsel appearing for the State- Opposite Party.
Perused the bail application as well as the documents annexed thereto.

3. The present bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S., 2023, corresponds to Section 439 of Cr.P.C., has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with S.T. Case No.53/21 of 2022-2025, arising out of Brahmanitarang P.S. Case No.96 of 2021, pending in the court of learned Adhoc Additional District and Sessions Judge (FTSC) (POCSO), Rourkela, for alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 376(1)/420/417/376(2)(n) of I.P.C.
4.

Rourkela in S.T. Case No.53/21 of 2022-2025 vide order dated 15.09.2021.

sentences.text: 5. A certified copy of order dated 15.09.2021 is filed in Court today.
The same is taken on record.
On perusal of the order dated 15.09.2021, it appears that the Petitioner was released on bail subject to the terms and conditions mentioned therein.

sentences.text: In course of his argument, learned counsel for the Petitioner further submitted that although the Petitioner was released on bail and was appearing before the trial court, however, he could not appear before the trial court on 07.01.2025.
Accordingly, an N.B.W. was issued against the Petitioner.
On execution of N.B.W. of arrest, the Petitioner was arrested and taken to custody on 16.10.2025.
Thereafter, the Petitioner moved an application for bail and the same has been rejected vide order dated 01.12.2025.
Being aggrieved by such order, the Petitioner approached this Court by filing present bail application.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that earlier the Petitioner was released on bail by the trial court.
He further submitted that due to the illness of the wife of the Petitioner and due to a communication gap with his conducting counsel, the Petitioner could not appear on the date the case was posted.
He further submitted that the Petitioner is languishing in jail custody since 16.10.2025.
He further submitted that the Petitioner is ready and willing to abide by any terms and condition as would be deemed just and proper by this Court in the event he is released on bail.

7. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that the Petitioner has already defaulted and because of the conduct of the Petitioner, he does not deserve any sympathy from this Court.

Learned counsel for the State further submitted that in the event the Petitioner is released on bail, there is every likelihood that he might abscond from justice which will cause delay in conclusion of the trial.
On such ground, it was submitted that the prayer for bail of the Petitioner be rejected at this juncture.

8. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and on a careful examination of the background facts as well as materials on record, further on consideration of order dated 15.09.2021, which is placed on record by the counsel for the Petitioner in Court today, it appears that the Petitioner was released on bail by the trial court subject to certain terms and conditions.

It also appears that the Petitioner has been arrested and he has languishing in jail custody since 16.10.2025.
9.

Considering the fact that the Petitioner was earlier released on bail and taking into consideration the undertaking that the Petitioner shall appear before the trial court on each and every date posting of the case without fail, this Court in inclined to release the Petitioner on bail.

10. Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the court in seisin over the matter.
The release of the Petitioner shall also be subject to such other terms and conditions as would be fixed by the court in seisin over the matter.

It is made clear that in the event any of the conditions are violated, it would be open to the trial court to take any coercive measures to ensure the presence of the Petitioner before the trial court.
11. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order as per Rules.
